findings.claim: A <div class="higher-only"> wrapper runs from the 'Bond Energy Calculations (Higher)' heading all the way past the closing Key Fact, so Foundation students never see 'Breaking bonds requires energy (endothermic). Making bonds releases energy (exothermic).'
findings.truth: Only the calculation is Higher Tier. The qualitative rule is not a bold statement, the specification lists 'energy is released when bonds break' as a common misconception to be addressed with all learners, and lesson 6 already teaches the same rule unwrapped to both tiers. Narrow the wrapper to close after the worked example and drop the now-wrong 'Higher tier:' from the Key Fact's revision tip.
findings.evidence: spec C3.2d is bold ('calculate energy changes in a chemical reaction by considering bond making and bond breaking energies'); C3.2a-c are not bold; C3.2 Common misconceptions; lesson 6 n21

findings.claim: Match check 'Match each reaction type to its temperature change in the surroundings': left Exothermic / Endothermic / Combustion, right 'Temperature increases' / 'Temperature decreases' / 'Temperature increases (releases heat)'.
findings.truth: Two right-hand options say the same thing, so a student who pairs Combustion with 'Temperature increases' is marked wrong for a correct answer. Make the third option distinct ('An exothermic reaction between a fuel and oxygen') and change the prompt to 'Match each term to its description:'.
findings.evidence: duplicated options in a match item; order [0,1,2] still holds after the change

findings.claim: The 4-mark bond energy question (N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3) and the third Key Takeaway give the bond energy method with no tier flag, while the article paragraph that teaches it is wrapped Higher.
findings.truth: C3.2d is bold, so both are Higher Tier only. Prefix '(Higher tier)'. The arithmetic itself is right: 945 + 3x436 = 2253 kJ broken, 6x391 = 2346 kJ made, 2253 - 2346 = -93 kJ, exothermic.
findings.evidence: spec C3.2d bold; recomputation of the worked answer

findings.claim: 'Each step on the pH scale represents a tenfold change in hydrogen ion concentration.' sits in an unflagged both-tier paragraph (n6).
findings.truth: C3.3j ('as hydrogen ion concentration increases by a factor of ten, the pH value decreases by one') is bold, so Foundation students are not tested on it. The identical fact already sits inside the Higher wrapper in the next section (n8), so the unflagged copy is removed rather than re-wrapped.
findings.evidence: spec C3.3j is bold; duplicate sentence at n8 inside the existing higher-only block

findings.claim: 'Oxidation is the gain of oxygen or the loss of electrons. Reduction is the loss of oxygen or the gain of electrons... A useful mnemonic is OIL RIG' - the electron definitions are given flat, with no tier flag.
findings.truth: C3.3a (oxygen) is both tiers; C3.3b (electrons) is bold and Higher Tier only. The next paragraph and the Key Fact do say 'At Higher Tier', so only the opening sentences need fixing: give the oxygen definitions first, then flag the electron definitions as Higher.
findings.evidence: spec C3.3a not bold, C3.3b bold

findings.claim: Two practice questions and three flashcards test bold statements with no tier flag: 'Explain, in terms of electron transfer, why 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO is a redox reaction' (C3.3b), the 6-mark electrolysis question that says 'Include half equations in your answer' (C3.4d), 'What is oxidation in terms of electrons?', 'What is reduction in terms of electrons?' and 'Write the cathode half equation for sodium ions.'
findings.truth: C3.3b and the 'half equations' clause of C3.4d (and of C3.1b) are bold. Prefix '(Higher tier)' on the practice questions and tag the flashcards at the end.
findings.evidence: spec C3.3b bold; C3.4d 'the equations and **half equations** of the reactions at the electrodes'

findings.claim: 'Write half equations for each electrode and state whether oxidation or reduction occurs.' is given as advice to every student.
findings.truth: Half equations are Higher Tier only. Say 'At Higher tier, write half equations...'.
findings.evidence: spec C3.4d, half equations in bold

findings.claim: 'atoms are rearranged in reactions but never created or destroyed (C3.1a)'.
findings.truth: C3.1a is 'use chemical symbols to write the formulae of elements and simple covalent and ionic compounds'. The law of conservation of mass is C3.1k.

findings.claim: 'OCR Gateway requires knowledge of several reaction types (C3.1b):' introducing combustion, displacement, neutralisation, redox and thermal decomposition.
findings.truth: C3.1b is about writing formulae and balanced chemical equations, not reaction types. Combustion, displacement and thermal decomposition are listed as prior knowledge for C3.3, neutralisation is C3.3d and redox is C3.3a, so no single code covers the list. The code is removed.
findings.evidence: spec C3.1b; C3.3 'Underlying knowledge and understanding'; C3.3a, C3.3d

findings.claim: 'One mole of any substance contains 6.022 x 10^23 particles, known as the _____ constant.' has no tier flag.
findings.truth: C3.1h ('recall and use the definitions of the Avogadro constant (in standard form) and of the mole') is bold, so this is Higher Tier only. The value itself is right. Prefix '(Higher tier)'.
findings.evidence: spec C3.1h bold; the specification states no numerical value, 6.022 x 10^23 mol-1 is the settled value

findings.claim: Six practice fields across lessons 6, 7 and 8 contain KaTeX delimiters, e.g. 'Calculate the relative formula mass of calcium carbonate (\(CaCO_3\))' and 'Balance the following equation: \(Fe + O_2 \rightarrow Fe_2O_3\)'.
findings.truth: The lesson page runs KaTeX only over the article, conclusion, exam tip, the knowledge-check modal and the flashcards. Practice question text is written with textContent and the mark scheme is not re-rendered, so students read the raw delimiters. Replaced with unicode formulae, matching the house style already used in the lesson 8 knowledge check ('2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO').
findings.evidence: js/lesson-loader.js renders KaTeX into study-notes, conclusion and exam-tip only; js/main.js line 459 sets practice text with textContent

findings.claim: Nine plain-text flashcard fields carry raw LaTeX: '\div' and 'R_f' twice and 'M_r' (lesson 3), 'C_{60}' (lesson 5), 'H_2O' (lesson 6), 'H^+', 'OH^-' and the whole half equation 'Na^+ + e^- \rightarrow Na.' (lesson 8).
findings.truth: Plain-text fields use unicode. The flashcard renderer only runs KaTeX on delimited maths, so these show literally. Converted to unicode.
findings.evidence: house rule: *_html fields use entities, plain-text fields use unicode

findings.claim: 'What is the approximate relative mass of an electron?' offers '1', '0', 'Very nearly zero (negligible)' and '-1', and marks only 'Very nearly zero (negligible)' right.
findings.truth: Many textbooks and classroom tables print the electron's relative mass as 0, so a student with the right idea is marked wrong by an option that means the same as the key. The '0' distractor is replaced by '1836', which catches the real error of quoting the mass ratio the wrong way round.
findings.evidence: spec C1.2d 'recall relative charges and approximate relative masses of protons, neutrons and electrons'; two options carry the same meaning

findings.claim: Lesson-to-paper mapping and coverage of C1-C3.
findings.truth: The mapping is correct and no lesson states a paper structure, so nothing needs correcting there: L1 C1.1, L2 C1.2, L3 C2.1, L4 C2.2, L5 C2.3, L6 C3.1, L7 C3.2, L8 C3.3 and C3.4 - exactly the content of Chemistry Paper 1 (Foundation Paper 3, Higher Paper 9), 1 hour 10 minutes, 60 marks, 16.7% of the qualification, with practical skills as PAGs C1-C5. Three coverage gaps need Tom's call. (a) C2.2i, how Mendeleev's arrangement was refined into the modern Periodic Table using atomic number, is taught in no lesson - it is a both-tier statement and lesson 4 already discusses the Periodic Table, so one paragraph there would close it. (b) The Higher mole cluster C3.1h, C3.1i, C3.1j and C3.1m (definitions of the mole and the Avogadro constant, mass to moles, concentration, stoichiometry and limiting reactants) is taught nowhere, although lesson 6's description promises 'the mole concept' and one knowledge check asks for the Avogadro constant; only C3.1n gets a worked example. (c) C3.1e, constructing balanced ionic equations, is not taught. Recommendation: add the Mendeleev paragraph to lesson 4 and a Higher-tier moles section to lesson 6, both as a separate build task rather than a fact-check edit.
findings.evidence: spec section 2a paper table; spec C2.2i, C3.1e, C3.1h, C3.1i, C3.1j, C3.1m

findings.claim: A flashcard asks 'What does a catalyst do to the activation energy?' (answer: lowers it by providing an alternative pathway).
findings.truth: The answer is correct, but catalysts are C5.2 in this specification, which sits in Chemistry Paper 2 (Foundation Paper 4, Higher Paper 10). It is out of scope for a Paper 1 lesson. Not edited because a flashcard cannot be deleted through the edit path and rewriting it is a content decision.
findings.evidence: spec C5 'describe the characteristics of catalysts'; Paper 2 covers C4-C6

findings.claim: 'all the energy goes into breaking or forming intermolecular forces, not raising the temperature' and 'energy is being used to break intermolecular forces'.
findings.truth: 'Intermolecular' is only right for simple molecular substances; melting an ionic or metallic solid breaks bonds, not intermolecular forces. The specification says 'forces of attraction between particles', and the lesson's own exam tip already says 'forces between particles'. Left alone because the lesson's examples are all molecular and the wording costs no marks at this level.

findings.claim: The limitations of the particle model are correctly wrapped Higher in the article, but the 6-mark practice question ('Discuss the usefulness and limitations of this model') and two flashcards ('Give one limitation of the simple particle model.', 'Why are inelastic spheres a weak model for real particles?') carry no tier flag.
findings.truth: C1.1c is bold, so all three are Higher Tier only. Prefix '(Higher tier)' on the practice question and tag the flashcards at the end. The Key Takeaway is left as it is: it summarises a limitation the article already flags, and it sets no Higher-only task.

summary: Eight lessons checked against OCR Gateway Combined Science A, Chemistry Paper 1 (Foundation Paper 3 / Higher Paper 9, topics C1-C3 plus PAGs C1-C5). Every worked calculation is right - relative formula masses, the Rf value, the 4.4 g of carbon dioxide, both bond energy sums, and every chemical equation balances - and no fact, definition, model or historical attribution is wrong. The damage is all tiering and plumbing: one higher-only wrapper is too wide and hides a both-tier Key Fact, two bold statements (the pH tenfold rule and electron-transfer redox) are taught unflagged, eleven questions and flashcards test bold statements with no tier tag, two spec codes in lesson 6 point at the wrong statements, a match check has two options that mean the same thing, an electron-mass check marks a defensible answer wrong, and fifteen plain-text question and flashcard fields carry LaTeX that the page never renders.
